questions.hint: Divide favorable outcomes by total outcomes.

stimulus.body: A fair coin is flipped 3 times. What is the probability of getting at least one head?

questions.stem: A fair coin is flipped 3 times. What is the probability of getting at least one head?

options.misconception: Wrong belief "gives the probability of all heads, not at least one" gives 1/8, not 7/8.
Wrong belief "divides one by the number of flips" gives 1/3, not 7/8.
Wrong belief "counts exactly one head instead of at least one" gives 3/8, not 7/8.

questions.explanation: The complement of at least one head is all tails, which has probability 1 over 2 to the 3; subtracting from 1 gives (2^3 minus 1) over 2^3, equal to 7/8.
questions.hint: Use the complement: one minus the probability of all tails.

questions.explanation: The complement of at least one head is all tails, which has probability 1 over 2 to the 5; subtracting from 1 gives (2^5 minus 1) over 2^5, equal to 31/32. The required result is 0.96875.
questions.hint: Use the complement: one minus the probability of all tails.

questions.stem: A bag contains 7 red and 5 blue marbles. One marble is drawn at random. What is the probability it is red?

questions.explanation: There are 7 favorable marbles among 12 total, so the probability of drawing red is 7/(12) which simplifies to 7/12.
